content: In France, public hospitals fully pay for care before and after birth through the national health system. Employed women can take 16 weeks of maternity leave and receive daily payments based on prior earnings, ranging from €9.29 to €84.90. During pregnancy and shortly after delivery, money troubles generally stay much the same as they were beforehand: families with limited means still face hardship, while richer families remain comfortable. But when it comes to practical support for new mothers, very little is provided. Fathers get just 11 days off, far too little to cover the mother’s recovery period. As a result, mothers are left to handle constant newborn care while also trying to recover physically. They must also look for childcare, even though public options are too limited, particularly around Paris. Costs differ widely: public daycare can be relatively affordable for poorer families, at about €1,000 a year, but spaces are extremely scarce, with only one spot for every eight children. Because of this shortage, many families turn to private options such as childminders or in-home care. Any other questions?
